To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parents of 7 year old children perceive that children’s oral health promoting behaviour is influenced by a number of factors, both at child, family, and community level.
parents’ views on influences on their children’s oral health are mainly related to the direct family environment.

parents perceive the most important influences on children’s dental health behaviours to be located at the level of the family, including parental confidence and knowledge about oral health, locus of control over children’s oral health, parental monitoring and role modelling of oral health behaviours, parenting strategies and routines, and the availability and affordability of healthy foods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical model to guide the development of effective oral health promotion interventions.
the development and evaluation of a new caries preventive programme for parents and children, the ‘Oral Health Promotion Programme’.
the identification of barriers and facilitation of oral health behaviours and professional oral health support in order to improve the oral health of Dutch and ethnic minority children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

parental support is a key factor in the promotion of children’s oral health, and that the development of interventions to promote children’s tooth brushing and dietary behaviours should include the involvement of parents.
parents’ suggestions for professional support to establish oral health promoting behaviours can be used to develop or improve caries preventive interventions.
the findings of this study can be used to improve the effectiveness of oral health promotion programmes and interventions for children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parents’ suggestions can help to develop and improve oral health promotion interventions for children.

the oral health of children is influenced by a variety of factors, both within and outside the family environment, and that parents would like more support from professionals in promoting children’s oral health.
oral health promoting interventions need to be developed and implemented in a holistic way, including the family, school and the social environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parents are a crucial resource for promoting oral health in children and that they should be actively involved in oral health promotion programmes.
oral health professionals should be aware that parents’ perceptions of the importance of oral health and their own confidence in tooth brushing are important influences on children’s behaviours.
parents are the most important agents for the promotion of children’s oral health.
